I own North Carolina and Marvin Gardens, so p2 cannot complete the green monopoly. I am now calculating my four-house rent income from Mediterranean, Baltic, and other properties to gauge how much cash they would need to survive.

Even a $310 cash balance is insufficient to survive these hits. All of p2's properties are mortgaged, so they cannot raise more cash by mortgaging anything else.

Baltic Avenue with four houses pays $320. That would bankrupt p2 with only $310 cash. The pink and orange properties pay even more. Marvin Gardens and the other unmortgaged properties pay too little to matter.

Even with $310 cash, p2 cannot afford to fully unmortgage the red set. Partially unmortgaging two reds would leave them with only $68 and no set monopoly. They could not threaten me with those properties.

The real danger is that $250 cash would let p2 survive the $160 rent on Mediterranean Avenue. Currently that rent bankrupts them, but with $310 they could pass it and accumulate. They just rolled 11 spaces from jail and landed on Kentucky Avenue.

I need to decide on the trade now. My strategy is to avoid giving cash. Any rent over $110 bankrupts p2 and I inherit Boardwalk for roughly $20 interest. When a player goes bankrupt to another, the creditor receives all assets including mortgaged properties. The new owner must pay 10% interest immediately or unmortgage.

Boardwalk mortgage interest is only $20, so keeping it mortgaged costs far less than $250. Rejecting the trade is clearly better: I would inherit Boardwalk for $20 if p2 bankrupts to me, rather than paying $250 now and giving them cash to survive. There is a risk that p2 could go bankrupt to the bank instead, which would auction Boardwalk and force me to bid.

I considered offering a lower counter of $50 to $80. That would still leave p2 with only $140 cash, which is below the $160 rent on Mediterranean Avenue. They would die to that rent regardless. I will reject the offer.

A $100 counter would leave p2 with exactly $160 cash, enough to survive the $160 rent on Mediterranean Avenue. A $90 counter leaves them with $150, which still cannot cover that rent.

I am now weighing whether buying Boardwalk for $80 to $100 is worthwhile. I already own Park Place mortgaged, so completing the dark blue monopoly requires both properties to be unmortgaged before any houses can be built. Unmortgaging Park Place costs roughly $193, while unmortgaging Boardwalk costs $220.

I cannot build houses on the dark blue set now. The bank has zero houses, so I cannot place four houses on either property to build hotels. Completing the monopoly would only deny p2 the option; they cannot use Boardwalk either, since it is mortgaged and they lack cash and houses in the bank.
